 Order

The instant petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Cr.P.C) has been filed by petitioners seeking quashing of the FIR bearing No. 213/2018, registered at Police Station Malviya Nagar, Delhi for the offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC) and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom.
2. Issue notice.
Mr. Manoj Pant, learned APP accepts notice on behalf of the State.

3. Petitioners nos. 1 and 2 are present before this Court and have been duly identified by their respective counsel, Mr. Sumit Kishore and Mr. Vineet Kumar Singh and Investigating Officer (IO) SI Saurabh from Police Station Malviya Nagar, Delhi.
4. Brief facts of the present case are that on 10.12.2016, the marriage was solemnized between petitioner no.1 and respondent no. 2, according to Hindu Rites and Ceremony.
No child was born out of the said wedlock.
Due to matrimonial disputes, the parties could not stay together and started living separately since 13.12.2016.

On the complaint of respondent no. 2, the present FIR bearing No. 213/2018 was registered at Police Station Malviya Nagar, Delhi for the offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of IPC against the petitioners.

It is stated that both the parties have amicably settled all their disputes before the court of learned Metropolitan Magistrate, Saket Courts, New Delhi where settlement statement was recorded on 30.08.2018 in Ct. No. 2211/2018.
6.

entities.text: Metropolitan Magistrate, Saket Courts, New Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: On a query made by this Court, respondent no. 2, who has been identified by the IO, has categorically stated that she has entered into a compromise out of her own free will and without any pressure, coercion or threat.

It is submitted that respondent no. 2 has settled all her claims in respect of her dowry articles, stridhan, marriage expenses, jewellery, gift items and claims of past,
present and future maintenance and permanent alimony with petitioner.

7. The petitioner no. 1 had paid a sum of Rs.12,00,000/- in three installments in the following manner:
a. First installment of Rs. 4,00,000/- paid to respondent no. 2 in the first motion petition.
b. Second installment of Rs. 4,00,000/- paid to respondent no. 2 in the second motion petition.
c. Third/Final installment of Rs. 4,00,000/- to be paid at the time of quashing of the present FIR before this court.

8. Today, the respondent no.2 who is present in Court states that she has received the last and final installment of Rs. 3,90,000/- today, vide DD No. 505487 drawn on ICICI Bank and a sum of Rs.10,000/- has been transferred to the bank account of the complainant through NEFT and that she has no objection if the FIR in question is quashed.

9. In view of the above facts that the parties have amicably resolved their differences out of their own free will and without any coercion and also the fact that the present matter is a family matter,
this Court is of the opinion that no useful purpose will be served by continuing the proceedings,
rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
Hence, it would be in the interest of justice to quash the abovementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
Moreover, there is no legal impediment in quashing the FIR in question.

10. Accordingly, FIR bearing No. 213/2018, registered at Police Station Malviya Nagar, Delhi for the offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of IPC and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
11. The present petition stands disposed of.
12. The order be uploaded on the website forthwith.
SWARANA KANTA SHARMA, J APRIL 20, 2023/j
